# Vella — drive and systems

Generated from the templates by `python3 lore/physics.py`; bracketed physics keys identify ledger claims, not spoken dialogue. Inputs, derived values and assumptions are separated in `../physics.json`. This is an operational fiction with an explicitly exotic field, not a claim that current physics permits this vessel.

## Known physics and engineering extrapolation

D–He3 fusion supplies heat and directed charged exhaust; D–D side reactions and neutrons remain shielding problems. The ledger's fusion conversion assumption is {{field.fusion_efficiency:.4f}} [physics:field.fusion_efficiency] of fuel rest energy, or {{field.fusion_energy_per_kg_J:.6e}} [physics:field.fusion_energy_per_kg_J] J/kg, with installed peak power {{field.fusion_power_W:.3e}} [physics:field.fusion_power_W] W. Sustained compact fusion propulsion, long-lived superconducting magnets, and reversible human cryosleep are unproved engineering/biology, not established present-day capabilities. Asterion precursor hardware made the old-universe first flight possible; no ordinary human programme possessed it in the launch era.

Wheels and stored electrical power move rover mode around people; there is no fusion exhaust in the garage or beside a cat. A remote pad and deployed cooling surfaces are prerequisites for any atmospheric torch burn. The atmosphere, passengers, permissions and heat footprint constrain it; the rover is not a licence to ignite a star indoors.

## The one exotic system: Asterion inertia field

Asterion reduces propulsion-coupled inertial mass inside its payload bubble by k, up to {{field.max_k:.0f}} [physics:field.max_k]; cruise holds k rather than switching it off at speed. The dry payload assumption {{field.ship_dry_kg:.0f}} [physics:field.ship_dry_kg] kg has effective inertial load {{field.effective_dry_kg:.3f}} [physics:field.effective_dry_kg] kg at maximum k. Its constitutive kinetic-work rule is Ekin=(gamma−unity)mc²/k: this is an admitted alteration of inertia/field dynamics, not a derivation from special relativity. The rest-energy offset is sequestered in the field state and cannot be tapped as electricity.

Simply scaling every mass in an ordinary closed rocket would leave its mass ratio unchanged. Asterion therefore also has a boundary reaction channel: momentum missing from the payload/exhaust ledger is carried by the exotic field and its external anchoring sector. That channel is part of the SAME field hypothesis; its microscopic stress-energy and anchoring origin are unknown, so I cannot certify a covariant theory or pretend the ordinary rocket equation was disproved. Fusion pays all positive mechanical work and control power; the boundary supplies no usable energy, and a closed field cycle must return no net work. Telemetry closes the operational energy account, not a fundamental proof of the field.

Control power is P=idle+coefficient×(k−unity): idle {{field.idle_W:.3e}} [physics:field.idle_W] W and coefficient {{field.W_per_k:.1f}} [physics:field.W_per_k] W per increment of k. Maximum control draw is {{field.max_control_W:.3e}} [physics:field.max_control_W] W; ramp time is {{field.ramp_seconds:.0f}} [physics:field.ramp_seconds] s. No setting allows v≥c; clock rates remain dτ=dt/gamma. Gravity's differential tidal acceleration is NOT cancelled: the rating across {{tidal.ship_span_m:.0f}} [physics:tidal.ship_span_m] m is {{tidal.rated_g:.1f}} [physics:tidal.rated_g] g. It does not erase radiation, collisions, heat or momentum transfer to the environment.

At the actual route peak, reduced-state dry-payload kinetic work is {{field.peak_effective_kinetic_J:.6e}} [physics:field.peak_effective_kinetic_J] J. Restoring ordinary inertia at that speed would require an additional {{field.restore_at_peak_J:.6e}} [physics:field.restore_at_peak_J] J: restoration is interlocked until near rest, and brownouts enter a separately charged passive hold state rather than magically restoring the hull at speed. Finite hold energy buys shutdown time; an exhausted hold reserve is a lethal failure, not a safe mode. Overload, asymmetric bubble coupling, magnet quench and field-boundary shear are distinct hazards. No emergency command cancels a tidal gradient.

A dry-payload acceleration/braking floor is {{field.mechanical_work_J:.6e}} [physics:field.mechanical_work_J] J; maximum-control operation throughout the route costs {{field.control_voyage_J:.6e}} [physics:field.control_voyage_J] J. Their fusion-fuel floor is {{field.minimum_fusion_fuel_kg:.3f}} [physics:field.minimum_fusion_fuel_kg] kg, excluding fuel self-transport, tanks, radiators, neutron losses, shielding, housekeeping and reserves. This lower bound is NOT a complete wet-mass or reactor feasibility claim. Observed field hardware is of unknown manufacture; its relationship to the woman on the rock remains a hook, not an answer or proof of who she is.

## Clocks: benchmark versus actual itinerary — captain-private

For acceleration {{constants.a_m_s2:.2f}} [physics:constants.a_m_s2] m/s² = {{constants.a_ly_yr2:.6f}} [physics:constants.a_ly_yr2] ly/yr², each four-burn reference uses eta=asinh(T/(four×c/a)); proper duration is four×(c/a)×eta. The outbound midpoint reverses acceleration, the distant turnaround is at rest, and the inward half repeats the profile. Rapidity increments add; neither a turnaround nor braking is instantaneous.

The first out-and-back reference takes {{trip1.earth_years:.0f}} [physics:trip1.earth_years] Earth years, {{trip1.ship_years:.6f}} [physics:trip1.ship_years] ship years, peaks at gamma {{trip1.peak_gamma:.6f}} [physics:trip1.peak_gamma] and beta {{trip1.peak_beta:.8f}} [physics:trip1.peak_beta], and turns {{trip1.turnaround_ly:.6f}} [physics:trip1.turnaround_ly] ly away. Each burn changes rapidity by {{trip1.rapidity_per_burn:.6f}} [physics:trip1.rapidity_per_burn]; biological aging is an ASSUMED {{trip1.awake_years:.1f}} [physics:trip1.awake_years] awake years after {{trip1.cryo_years:.6f}} [physics:trip1.cryo_years] cryo years.

The second four-burn REFERENCE takes {{trip2.earth_years:.0f}} [physics:trip2.earth_years] Earth years, {{trip2.ship_years:.6f}} [physics:trip2.ship_years] ship years, peaks at gamma {{trip2.peak_gamma:.6f}} [physics:trip2.peak_gamma] and beta {{trip2.peak_beta:.8f}} [physics:trip2.peak_beta], and turns {{trip2.turnaround_ly:.6f}} [physics:trip2.turnaround_ly] ly away. Each burn changes rapidity by {{trip2.rapidity_per_burn:.6f}} [physics:trip2.rapidity_per_burn]; reference cryo is {{trip2.cryo_years:.6f}} [physics:trip2.cryo_years] years for assumed awake aging {{trip2.awake_years:.1f}} [physics:trip2.awake_years] years. This reference does NOT describe a route visiting several non-collinear stars.

The constructive actual itinerary uses rest-to-rest catalogue legs Sol→Proxima→Alpha Centauri→Luhman, then a fictional outward detour and return toward the binary. Their distances are {{route.legs.proxima.distance_ly:.6f}} [physics:route.legs.proxima.distance_ly], {{route.legs.alpha.distance_ly:.6f}} [physics:route.legs.alpha.distance_ly], {{route.legs.luhman.distance_ly:.6f}} [physics:route.legs.luhman.distance_ly], {{route.legs.turn.distance_ly:.6f}} [physics:route.legs.turn.distance_ly] and {{route.legs.binary.distance_ly:.6f}} [physics:route.legs.binary.distance_ly] ly. The detour lies opposite the binary across Luhman; the binary and probe remain approximately {{route.binary_offset_from_luhman_ly:.1f}} [physics:route.binary_offset_from_luhman_ly] ly from Luhman. No visit to the thousand-light-year-away Vela Pulsar is implied.

Total actual travel is {{route.travel_earth_years:.6f}} [physics:route.travel_earth_years] Earth years, plus {{route.local_dwell_years:.6f}} [physics:route.local_dwell_years] years of local repairs/dwell to reach the same Earth duration. Actual ship time is {{route.ship_years:.6f}} [physics:route.ship_years] years, actual peak gamma {{route.peak_gamma:.6f}} [physics:route.peak_gamma], and actual cryo {{route.cryo_years:.6f}} [physics:route.cryo_years] years for {{route.awake_years:.1f}} [physics:route.awake_years] awake years. This replaces the old approximate ship-clock/gamma account; it does not change the captain's rounded biological age. The final dwell is local, so Earth and ship clocks advance approximately together; the small local assist correction is not a hidden interstellar leg.

## Rocket equation — what an ordinary rocket cannot afford

For an ordinary isolated ideal rocket, ln R=delta-eta×c/v_e. Exhaust-speed assumptions are chemical {{rocket.trip1.chemical.exhaust_beta:.8f}} [physics:rocket.trip1.chemical.exhaust_beta] c, Orion {{rocket.trip1.orion.exhaust_beta:.2f}} [physics:rocket.trip1.orion.exhaust_beta] c, Daedalus-like fusion {{rocket.trip1.daedalus.exhaust_beta:.2f}} [physics:rocket.trip1.daedalus.exhaust_beta] c, optimistic fusion {{rocket.trip1.best_fusion.exhaust_beta:.1f}} [physics:rocket.trip1.best_fusion.exhaust_beta] c and photon {{rocket.trip1.photon.exhaust_beta:.1f}} [physics:rocket.trip1.photon.exhaust_beta] c; these are comparison assumptions, not measured performance of named historic projects.

The first reference needs delta-eta {{trip1.one_way_delta_eta:.6f}} [physics:trip1.one_way_delta_eta] one-way and {{trip1.round_trip_delta_eta:.6f}} [physics:trip1.round_trip_delta_eta] round-trip. Daedalus-like one-way R is exp({{rocket.trip1.daedalus.one_way_ln_R:.6f}} [physics:rocket.trip1.daedalus.one_way_ln_R]); even photon exhaust gives R={{rocket.trip1.photon.one_way_R:.3f}} [physics:rocket.trip1.photon.one_way_R] one-way and {{rocket.trip1.photon.round_trip_R:.3f}} [physics:rocket.trip1.photon.round_trip_R] round-trip. The second reference photon ratios are {{rocket.trip2.photon.one_way_R:.3f}} [physics:rocket.trip2.photon.one_way_R] and {{rocket.trip2.photon.round_trip_R:.3f}} [physics:rocket.trip2.photon.round_trip_R]. The full chemical/Orion/fusion table is in the ledger, using logarithms when exponentials overflow. Asterion is a stated exception to closed-rocket dynamics; fusion alone is not an answer to these ratios.

## Gas, grains and shields

Ambient density assumption: {{medium.trip2.density_low_cm3:.1f}} [physics:medium.trip2.density_low_cm3]–{{medium.trip2.density_high_cm3:.1f}} [physics:medium.trip2.density_high_cm3] particles/cm³ in the old-star frame, treated as protons. Ship-frame flux is gamma×n×v, not merely n×v. At the second REFERENCE peak a proton carries {{medium.trip2.proton_GeV:.6f}} [physics:medium.trip2.proton_GeV] GeV; flux is {{medium.trip2.flux_low_m2_s:.6e}} [physics:medium.trip2.flux_low_m2_s]–{{medium.trip2.flux_high_m2_s:.6e}} [physics:medium.trip2.flux_high_m2_s] per m²/s. An illustrative ionisation-only unshielded dose is {{medium.trip2.dose_low_Gy_day:.6e}} [physics:medium.trip2.dose_low_Gy_day]–{{medium.trip2.dose_high_Gy_day:.6e}} [physics:medium.trip2.dose_high_Gy_day] Gy/day using {{medium.trip2.stopping_MeV_per_g_cm2:.1f}} [physics:medium.trip2.stopping_MeV_per_g_cm2] MeV/(g/cm²). This is not Sv, not a detailed human-dose prediction, and excludes hadronic cascades; it already rules out an exposed passenger.

A grain of {{medium.trip2.dust_microgram:.0f}} [physics:medium.trip2.dust_microgram] microgram has second-reference kinetic energy {{medium.trip2.dust_J:.6e}} [physics:medium.trip2.dust_J] J = {{medium.trip2.dust_tonnes_TNT:.6f}} [physics:medium.trip2.dust_tonnes_TNT] tonnes TNT. At the first peak it is {{medium.trip1.dust_J:.6e}} [physics:medium.trip1.dust_J] J = {{medium.trip1.dust_tonnes_TNT:.6f}} [physics:medium.trip1.dust_tonnes_TNT] tonnes. The actual itinerary's higher peak must not be hidden: protons are {{medium.route.proton_GeV:.6f}} [physics:medium.route.proton_GeV] GeV and that grain is {{medium.route.dust_J:.6e}} [physics:medium.route.dust_J] J = {{medium.route.dust_tonnes_TNT:.6f}} [physics:medium.route.dust_tonnes_TNT] tonnes.

The stack is upstream detection and grain ablation/dispersal, gas ionisation, magnetic deflection, electrostatic cleanup, and sacrificial layered absorbers backed by water/secondary-particle shielding. Neutral grains do not politely follow magnetic field lines. The assumed {{shield.magnetic_B_T:.0f}} [physics:shield.magnetic_B_T] T across {{shield.magnetic_length_m:.0f}} [physics:shield.magnetic_length_m] m gives {{shield.rigidity_Tm:.1f}} [physics:shield.rigidity_Tm] T·m, versus actual peak proton rigidity {{medium.route.proton_rigidity_Tm:.6f}} [physics:medium.route.proton_rigidity_Tm] T·m; that comparison is necessary, not a proof of collection geometry or survival. A direct unresolved grain strike can still destroy the vessel.

The percent gauge measures deposited thermal load plus shield-control dissipation, not all incident beam energy. Deflected particles carry most of their energy away; it is not all deposited in the hull. The percent gauge uses {{shield.reference_W:.3e}} [physics:shield.reference_W] W as its REFERENCE, not its limit. The Proxima event was {{shield.event_percent:.0f}} [physics:shield.event_percent] percent = {{shield.event_W:.3e}} [physics:shield.event_W] W for {{shield.event_seconds:.0f}} [physics:shield.event_seconds] s, total {{shield.event_J:.6e}} [physics:shield.event_J] J. Rated continuous handling is {{shield.rated_W:.3e}} [physics:shield.rated_W] W = {{shield.rated_percent:.0f}} [physics:shield.rated_percent] percent on that scale: the event used {{shield.rated_utilization_percent:.1f}} [physics:shield.rated_utilization_percent] percent of rating and retained {{shield.rated_margin_W:.3e}} [physics:shield.rated_margin_W] W margin. Safe on the recorded scale, visibly serious; no claim that a grain detonated inside the shield or that this was the voyage's peak-gamma encounter.

## Heat rejection

Fusion exhaust removes useful directed energy; reactor waste, magnet losses and intercepted particles still require cooling. Assumed emissivity {{radiator.emissivity:.2f}} [physics:radiator.emissivity], temperature {{radiator.temperature_K:.0f}} [physics:radiator.temperature_K] K and waste heat {{radiator.waste_heat_W:.3e}} [physics:radiator.waste_heat_W] W imply {{radiator.surface_W_m2:.6e}} [physics:radiator.surface_W_m2] W/m² and {{radiator.emitting_area_m2:.3f}} [physics:radiator.emitting_area_m2] m² of emitting surface by Stefan–Boltzmann. That is total emitting area, not necessarily panel footprint; deployed radiators are large and fragile. A closed garage cannot sustain this operating point. A hypothetical residual deposition fraction {{shield.residual_fraction:.3f}} [physics:shield.residual_fraction] over frontal area {{shield.frontal_m2:.0f}} [physics:shield.frontal_m2] m² at actual high-density peak adds {{shield.peak_residual_heat_W:.6e}} [physics:shield.peak_residual_heat_W] W; that fraction is an engineering assumption, not a validated transport result.

## NSB-Rook-A/B incident — captain-private

NSB-Rook-A/B is a fictional cold, previously uncatalogued binary, not a real claimed nearby discovery; known nearby neutron stars are hundreds of light-years away. Each model component has mass {{tidal.ns_mass_solar:.1f}} [physics:tidal.ns_mass_solar] solar masses and separation {{tidal.binary_separation_km:.0f}} [physics:tidal.binary_separation_km] km, giving component speed {{tidal.binary_component_speed_km_s:.3f}} [physics:tidal.binary_component_speed_km_s] km/s. We planned a moving-body scatter plus a powered periapsis correction, exchanging orbital energy rather than manufacturing fuel. Poor binary phase/ephemeris prediction and a failed correction displaced the component-relative periapsis from {{tidal.planned_radius_km:.0f}} [physics:tidal.planned_radius_km] km to {{tidal.actual_radius_km:.0f}} [physics:tidal.actual_radius_km] km.

Across the ship span, the radial approximation gives {{tidal.planned_g:.6f}} [physics:tidal.planned_g] g planned versus {{tidal.actual_g:.6f}} [physics:tidal.actual_g] g actual. The conservative single-component rating requires radius at least {{tidal.minimum_radius_km:.3f}} [physics:tidal.minimum_radius_km] km; binary terms and GR would require additional margin. For comparison, at a thousand km it is {{tidal.at_1000_km_g:.6f}} [physics:tidal.at_1000_km_g] g and at fifty km {{tidal.at_50_km_g:.6e}} [physics:tidal.at_50_km_g] g. These are gradients, not the common free-fall acceleration that an accelerometer subtracts.

Boundary shear tore the navigation and drive compartments: Pavel and Imani died immediately, Leena died sealing coolant, and Hana later died after her medical cryosupport and oxygen failed. Rook's separate surviving berth made later low-demand cryosleep possible. Asterion maintained bulk inertia reduction; it did not cancel the killing gradient. The trajectory correction pointed toward Luhman but left the vessel near the binary, still about the recorded probe distance away; it did not cross that interstellar distance during the local repair interval. The later solo recovery attempt was local and nearly killed him again.

## Signals, air and unknown transit — captain-private

For the old-Earth impact {{signal.impact_after_departure_days:.0f}} [physics:signal.impact_after_departure_days] days after departure, the accelerating-ship light intersection is {{signal.received_after_departure_days:.6f}} [physics:signal.received_after_departure_days] days after launch. Signal delay is {{signal.delay_days:.6f}} [physics:signal.delay_days] days; receiver distance is {{signal.receiver_distance_AU:.6f}} [physics:signal.receiver_distance_AU] AU. News arrived after departure, not instantaneously from interstellar range. Luhman↔probe signalling alone takes {{signal.probe_to_luhman_years:.0f}} [physics:signal.probe_to_luhman_years] years each way absent the unexplained transit.

Salvage restored reclamation power, not oxygen nuclei from electricity. Service {{air.service_hours:.0f}} [physics:air.service_hours] h = {{air.service_days:.6f}} [physics:air.service_days] days for the remaining occupant corresponds to {{air.oxygen_one_kg:.3f}} [physics:air.oxygen_one_kg] kg metabolic oxygen throughput at {{air.oxygen_kg_person_day:.2f}} [physics:air.oxygen_kg_person_day] kg/person/day. The same unreplenished oxygen serves the initial crew for {{air.same_oxygen_five_hours:.0f}} [physics:air.same_oxygen_five_hours] h; full service for that crew needs {{air.oxygen_five_kg:.3f}} [physics:air.oxygen_five_kg] kg throughput. Recovered water/CO₂ processing, feedstock, filters and leaks constrain the service estimate. Only {{route.salvage_to_transit_days:.0f}} [physics:route.salvage_to_transit_days] local days remain between salvage and transit, so the recovered service budget covers them even without claiming free cryo air.

A kilometre-class impact can end the already fragile remaining civilisation without gravitationally breaking Earth or sterilising every organism; “Earth destroyed” is that loss, not a computed total-biosphere extinction.

Morris–Thorne-type traversable wormholes require exotic stress, including negative energy density for standard examples and null-energy-condition violation; usable macroscopic matter of that kind is not known to exist. I have entry/exit sensor records, not a theory or a wormhole engine. Asterion's unknown origin does not establish that it opened the transit; this is an observed mystery outside the onboard-system specification. No known cause establishes why the room's sky differs, or why atmosphere exit is safe.
